text:
maya: Heads-up — we need a deprecation/migration plan for the old proxy shim (json->grpc translator) before we flip the protocol-router. Key concerns: query routing rules, per-route quotas, preserving tracing context, and tidy rollback paths. Thoughts? @tom @jess

Tom: Can we keep the shim as an adapter for a while? Main tradeoffs are extra latency + maintenance vs safer migration.

jess: If we keep it, we need telemetry showing error spikes and perf deltas per route. Also the Console must expose per-route rollout controls and a clear 'fallback' toggle.

ajay: Sidecar/BFF reduces central coupling and helps tenant-scoped quotas, but ups the ops surface. Sidecars are nice if traffic is very uneven across tenants. Otherwise a gateway-router with tenant routing is cheaper.

maya: Proposed rollout plan: 1) implement protocol-router that can speak JSON and gRPC (multi-proto) 2) run it in passthrough mode behind existing proxy 3) enable canary (5% of routes/users) with detailed metrics 4) after 2 weeks with no regressions, deprecate shim.

Tom: Per-route quotas require mapping path -> route-id early. Header approach looks simplest: add `x-rw-route-id` during routing so downstream components (quotas + telemetry) can attribute correctly.

jess: Example header + canary curl (quick sketch):

```
# mark request as canary 5% group
curl -H "x-rw-route-id: search.v2" -H "x-rw-canary: 5" https://api.internal.redwood/search?q=foo
```

Also we should show a small badge in Console when a route is in canary and the % slider.

eva: Metric names to track: `rw.requests.total`, `rw.requests.latency.p50`, `rw.requests.latency.p95`, `rw.fallback.count`. Traces: propagate `traceparent` or `x-cloud-trace-context` and include `route_id` as span attribute. Add an alert if fallback rate > 0.5% for 10m.

deploy-bot: deploy started: protocol-router v2 -> canary 5% @3344556699

ajay: Ops note — run the canary for at least 72h and simulate tenant spikes. Add a fast rollback: if we detect error rate spike or latency regression, switch incoming traffic to old shim by setting `x-rw-fallback: on` at the ingress layer, then follow up with an automated rollback.

Tom: Also need schema compatibility checks on the router. If the incoming JSON has unknown required fields or strongly typed mismatches for proto routes, return `422` with a helpful message instead of silently mapping. We should run `protoc`-based lint in CI and a runtime guard in the router.

jess: UX ask: Console should expose per-route rollout slider (0-100%), a small chart with latency & error delta vs baseline, and a one-click fallback toggle. Will mock a design and share tomorrow. :thumbsup:

maya: Sounds good — I'll file an RFC today and assign owners: @ajay for rollout automation/ops runbook, @tom for protocol-router and adapter code, @jess for Console/telemetry UX. I'll include acceptance criteria: no increased p95 > 10% for any route, fallback < 0.5% after 72h, and trace propagation validated.

Tom: Quick note — when we remove shim, remember to keep a compatibility endpoint for a month for some external partners. We can gate it behind an entitlement flag.

maya: Great point. We'll add a sunset list + partner communication step to the RFC.

jess: I'll add a small dashboard mock and the Console control flows to the RFC doc.

ajay: I'll prepare a runbook script to flip `x-rw-fallback` at the edge and a k8s job to scrub the header on the old shim for safety.

deploy-bot: canary metrics check at 3344556703: no error spike, p95 +3% vs baseline.

maya: Thanks — moving to RFC and owner assignment.
